title: Insulation Rebates in Sacramento 2026: Up to $3,000 from SMUD | HomePowerRebate
desc: SMUD's Seal and Insulate package pays up to $3,000 for air sealing and insulation through a Home Performance contractor. Who qualifies, how phasing works and steps.
lead: SMUD's Seal and Insulate package pays up to $3,000 through a Home Performance Program contractor. SMUD does not publish a per-square-foot price on its page, so this page covers who qualifies, how the five-year window works and what to ask before you book.
cards_intro: These figures come from SMUD's Home Performance Program page, which we read on October 2, 2026. Rebates depend on available funding and must be submitted by a qualified participating contractor in the SMUD Contractor Network. Applications are first come, first served.

cards.title: Seal and Insulate package
cards.note: Air sealing and added insulation, through a Home Performance Program contractor.

cards.title: Single-family, townhomes and condos
cards.note: These dwellings qualify for the full Seal and Insulate rebate.

cards.title: Duplexes to quadplexes
cards.note: Each unit with an attached attic, up to four units and attics per building.

cards.title: Not eligible
cards.note: Apartment complexes of more than four units and mobile homes do not qualify.

after_cards:
What we could not confirm

SMUD's page names the package and the $3,000 ceiling but does not list the per-measure amounts or the R-value targets in the part we could read. We do not quote a rate. Ask your Home Performance contractor for the written scope and the rebate that applies to it before you sign.
sections: You can do it in phases

SMUD says you do not have to do every upgrade at once, as long as you finish the whole project within five years of the first application. Its example: replace a broken furnace now, and add attic insulation or a water heater later. That matters for a household with a limited budget, because it means a failing heat pump swap does not close off the insulation rebate. Keep every document from the first application, since the five-year clock starts there.

SMUD's page says air sealing and adding insulation are often the most cost-effective ways to improve a home's efficiency, and it names heating and cooling as roughly 40% of a home's energy use. Air sealing stops the leaks that insulation cannot, around attic hatches, recessed lights, plumbing and wiring penetrations. Ask the contractor for a before and after test of the leaks, and for the insulation level you will reach in writing.

SMUD runs this through its Home Performance Program, so you cannot hire any insulation company and claim it. Customers can contact Advanced Home Solutions at 916-732-5732, and SMUD says your contractor is your first point of contact for the status of an application. SMUD's XeroHome tool gives energy upgrade recommendations. Sacramento's average January low over 2015 to 2024 was 4.7°C, and summers are hot, so attic insulation pays most in summer cooling.
Do it before you size a heat pump

An insulated, sealed attic lets you buy a smaller heating and cooling system, which costs less to buy and run. If you are planning a heat pump, have the insulation done first or ask your contractor to size the system for the finished house. SMUD's Home Performance Program bundles these steps so a single contractor can plan them together. See Sacramento heat pump rebates.
The federal 25C and 25D tax credits ended after December 31, 2025. SMUD's rebate is the main source of insulation money for Sacramento homes today.
claim_heading: How to claim the SMUD rebate
claim_steps: Confirm that SMUD is your electric utility and that your home is a single-family home, townhome, condo, or a two to four unit building.
Find a participating Home Performance Program contractor in the SMUD Contractor Network.
Ask the contractor to recommend an upgrade package and to put the scope and rebate in writing.
The contractor completes the work and submits the rebate on your behalf.
If you plan other upgrades, finish the whole project within five years of the first application.
Track the application through your contractor, then through the email SMUD sends once it is in the system.
faq: How much does SMUD pay for insulation?
Up to $3,000 for the Seal and Insulate package, through a participating Home Performance Program contractor.
Can I do it in stages?
Yes. SMUD says you can complete the project in phases as long as it is finished within five years of the first application.
Single-family homes, townhomes and condos get the full rebate. Duplexes to quadplexes get 50% per unit with an attic. Mobile homes and buildings over four units do not qualify.
Can I hire my own insulation company?
The rebate is submitted by a participating contractor in the SMUD Contractor Network, so choose a contractor from SMUD's list.
How do I track my rebate?
Your contractor is the first point of contact. Once the application is in SMUD's system you receive an email with instructions.
